title.value: Rapid, automated nerve histomorphometry through open‐source artificial intelligence
title.justification: The title clearly states the focus of the paper which is on utilizing open-source artificial intelligence for nerve histomorphometry. It does not mention climate or ecological sustainability, indicating this paper falls outside these contexts.
title.quote: Rapid, automated nerve histomorphometry through open‐source artificial intelligence

extractions.description: The paper discusses the development and validation of a deep learning model for the automated segmentation and histomorphometry of myelinated peripheral nerve fibers. It highlights the use of a convolutional neural network in the AxonDeepSeg framework to achieve accurate axon/myelin segmentation from light microscopic images, reducing analysis time significantly compared to manual methods. This open-source tool enhances the efficiency and precision of biomedical research related to nerve fiber analysis.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper primarily focuses on medical and biomedical applications related to nerve fiber analysis using deep learning frameworks. While it discusses advancements in automation and efficiency in the biomedical field, it does not address climate or ecological sustainable development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: We aimed to develop and validate a deep learning model for automated segmentation and histomorphometry of myelinated peripheral nerve fibers from light microscopic images.

primary_category.justification: The central theme of this paper is biomedical and neuroscience-focused, with no direct relation to climate or ecological sustainable development. It discusses a technological improvement in nerve histomorphometry using AI.
primary_category.quote: Given its easy applicability, it could contribute to significant time savings in biomedical research while extracting unprecedented amounts of objective morphologic information from large image datasets.

secondary_categories.justification: There are no secondary themes in the paper related to climate or ecological sustainable development. The entire focus is on the biomedical application of AI in nerve fiber analysis.
secondary_categories.quote: Axon diameter, myelin sheath thickness, and g-ratio are key metrics for clinicians and researchers alike. They are frequently used for diagnosis and staging of neuropathic ­diseases.

primary_sub_category.justification: There are no sub-categories within climate or ecological sustainable development that apply to this paper as its subject is entirely outside those domains, focused solely on medical AI applications.
primary_sub_category.quote: The model was trained for automated axon/myelin segmentation using a dataset of light-microscopic cross-sectional images of osmium tetroxide-stained rat nerves.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The paper does not cover any secondary sub-categories related to climate or ecological sustainable development. It's centered on improving efficiency and accuracy in nerve fiber segmentation using AI, which falls under medical research.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: This open-source convolutional neural network provides rapid and accurate morphometry of entire peripheral nerve cross-sections.

applications.justification: The specific application discussed is the automation of nerve fiber segmentation and morphometry through deep learning, enhancing efficiency and precision in biomedical research.
applications.quote: The neural network achieved high pixel-wise accuracy for nerve fiber segmentations with a mean (± standard deviation) ground truth overlap of 0.93 (± 0.03) for axons and 0.99 (± 0.01) for myelin sheaths, respectively.
